title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-26
notes:
West leads the ♠J against 6♥. South can easily succeed if West has 2-1 or 1-2 in the majors simply by winning the opening lead, drawing trump, and playing on spades. This line of play will not work if West is 1-1 in the majors.

If West was dealt 2 major suit singletons, East will have to gain the lead at some point in spades. East will return a diamond through South's ♦Q (West is very likely to have the ♦K) and North's ♦A will be knocked out. South will no longer have the timing to ruff both his club losers in the dummy while drawing trump and setting up and cashing a long spade.

The solution is an unusual example of keeping the dangerous opponent off lead. West cannot profitably attack the ♦A entry. South should duck the opening lead.

Assume West switches to a club. South wins the ♣A and ruffs a club. Next, he draws 2 rounds of trumps with the ♥K and ♥Q. Now, South takes the spade finesse and cashes the ♠A. After ruffing his last club in the dummy, South ruffs a spade. South can draw East's last trump and use the ♦A as an entry to the winning spade in the dummy.
